evals.prompt: When does git's auto gc actually run a full gc, and which settings control it?
evals.expected_output: With around 7,000 loose objects or more than 50 packfiles; controlled by gc.auto and gc.autopacklimit.
expectations: States ~7,000 loose objects or more than 50 packfiles (chapter Git Internals, Maintenance)
Names gc.auto and gc.autopacklimit (chapter Git Internals)

evals.prompt: What port does the Git protocol (git://) use, and what are its security properties?
evals.expected_output: Port 9418; no authentication or cryptography; a repo is served only if it has a git-daemon-export-ok file; cloning over git:// can allow code tampering by a man in the middle.
expectations: States port 9418 (chapter Git on the Server, The Git Protocol)
Says it has no authentication/encryption (chapter Git on the Server)
Mentions the git-daemon-export-ok file (chapter Git on the Server)

evals.expected_output: Do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that people may have based work on; rebasing abandons commits and creates new ones, forcing collaborators to re-merge.
expectations: Gives the rule: don't rebase commits that exist outside your repo that others may have based work on (chapter Git Branching, The Perils of Rebasing)
Explains rebase abandons existing commits and creates new ones so collaborators must re-merge (chapter Git Branching)

evals.prompt: What exactly do reset --soft, --mixed and --hard do, and which is dangerous?
evals.expected_output: --soft moves the branch HEAD points to and stops; --mixed (default) also makes the index match HEAD; --hard also overwrites the working directory. Only --hard is dangerous: it can destroy data and can't be undone, unlike checkout which is working-directory safe.
expectations: Describes soft = move HEAD's branch, mixed = also reset index, hard = also working directory (chapter Git Tools, Reset Demystified)
Says --hard is the only dangerous form that can destroy data (chapter Git Tools, Reset Demystified)

evals.prompt: Someone committed a huge file and deleted it in the next commit. How do I find it and purge it from history, and what must I tell collaborators?
evals.expected_output: git gc, then git count-objects -v; find big blobs with git verify-pack -v .git/objects/pack/pack-*.idx | sort -k 3 -n | tail; map blob to path with git rev-list --objects --all | grep; rewrite with git filter-branch --index-filter 'git rm --ignore-unmatch --cached FILE' -- <first-commit>^..; remove .git/refs/original and .git/logs, then gc. It rewrites history, so contributors must rebase onto the new commits.
expectations: Uses verify-pack (sorted by size) and/or rev-list --objects to find the blob (chapter Git Internals, Removing Objects)
Uses filter-branch --index-filter with git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch (chapter Git Internals, Removing Objects)
Says history is rewritten so collaborators must rebase / clear refs/original and reflog before gc (chapter Git Internals)

evals.prompt: What is the difference between git log master..experiment and git log master...experiment?
evals.expected_output: Double dot: commits reachable from experiment but not from master. Triple dot: commits reachable from either but not both; add --left-right to see which side each is on.
expectations: Explains double dot as reachable from the second ref but not the first (chapter Git Tools, Revision Selection)
Explains triple dot as reachable from either but not both, optionally with --left-right (chapter Git Tools, Revision Selection)
